content: (The location is now Solitude.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Bliss, Solitude Guard, Frea, Cassie, Serana) (Cassie hit MJR with Ebony Sword)
Lydia: By Dibella's grace, get away from my Thane, you wench! I'll cleave you in two!
Imperial Soldier: Stand down, all of you! No brawling in Solitude this early morn!

Lydia: Stay out of this, Imperial dog! This bandit's after my Thane—I'll end her now in Dibella's name! Imperial Soldier: I said stand down, housecarl! Jarl Elisif won't have her city turned into a battlefield over some tavern scrap!

Lydia: My Thane's safety comes first, you Imperial lapdog! This slut struck him—feel the bite of my Ebony steel for Solitude's sake! Imperial Soldier: Enough! Guards, seize that housecarl before she turns this tavern into a bloodbath under the morning sky!

Lydia: That frostbow bitch Aline and her crossbow cronies won't touch my Thane again—by Dibella's curves, I'll smash their skulls in this Solitude shithole before dawn breaks fully! Imperial Soldier: The hells have broken loose in here with all this clanging steel and bolts flying! Lay off the fight, warrior—Jarl's orders demand peace in her halls, or it'll be chains for all of ya under this clear morning sky!

(*You are observing the following:* In the scene, a dimly lit stone chamber unfolds before you, with rough-hewn walls of gray rock adorned by flickering torchlight casting long shadows. Cobwebs drape from the ceiling, and a heavy wooden door stands slightly ajar at the far end, revealing a glimpse of an outdoor courtyard paved with cracked stone slabs under a twilight sky. Scattered on the floor are remnants of ancient debris—shards of pottery, a rusted iron chain, and a small wooden crate overturned near a corner. To the right, a narrow alcove holds a simple stone altar with faded runes etched into its surface, beside which lies a coiled rope and a leather-bound book. In the foreground, your view centers on a sturdy wooden table cluttered with alchemical vials, a half-eaten loaf of bread, and a gleaming metal crossbow propped against its edge, its string taut and bolt chambered. Overlaid across the vista are translucent command lines and status notifications in a crisp, glowing font: messages about loading a rugged warrior figure, flushing combat states with a companion named Cass, and tallying events in a log that reads "Added 15 events, max total in 5.) (Lydia is no longer in combat.) (Imperial Soldier is now in combat!) (MJR: I have a message from the Greybeards.; General Tullius: The Greybeards? What do those old hermits want with me?) (MJR: They're convening a peace council at High Hrothgar.; General Tullius: Why? There's nothing to discuss as long as that traitor Ulfric is in arms against his rightful Emperor.) (MJR: We need a truce until the dragon menace is dealt with.; General Tullius: They are getting to be a problem. But I wasn't sent to Skyrim to fight dragons. My job is to quell this rebellion, and I intend to do just that, dragons or no dragons.) (MJR: The dragons are a bigger problem than the Stormcloaks right now. (Persuade); General Tullius: Well, you may have a point. It's getting difficult to even move troops around without attracting a dragon attack. By all accounts the Stormcloaks are suffering just as badly. Even Ulfric might see the sense of a truce under these conditions.) (MJR: You'll come to the peace council, then?; General Tullius: Yes. Yes, fine, I'll come to this Greybeard council. For all the good it will do.) (The location is now Solitude.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Imperial Soldier, Daegon, Serana, Legate Rikke, General Tullius)

Imperial Soldier: Peace council with Ulfric? That dog doesn't deserve a truce, not after what he did at the Markarth incident. Solitude Guard: Dragons don't care about your politics, soldier. I've seen three villages burned this past week alone. If this Dragonborn can make both sides see reason, then so be it.
